sections.title: Your Echo collection record
paragraphs: The Data Bank is accessed from the Terminal and records collected Echoes. Raising it affects Echo acquisition parameters and progression rewards. GameBreak planning suggestion: check the collection list for an undiscovered Echo or a missing higher rarity, pick one reachable target, and verify the record after absorption. This is more informative than repeatedly farming a familiar enemy without knowing which entry is missing.

sections.title: Experience is not the same as item level
paragraphs: New Echo discoveries and newly recorded higher rarities can provide Data Bank experience. Recording a higher rarity also accounts for missing lower-rarity records of that Echo. This collection progression is distinct from spending materials to level an equipped Echo. Read the level panel for your account’s actual rates and restrictions; an old screenshot’s cap is not a reliable current target.

sections.title: Finding the system and handling duplicates
paragraphs: The community record places the Data Bank unlock in the early Prologue quest Utterance of Marvels: II. Data Merge is a related inventory system: it consumes eligible Echoes to produce a random result, whose rarity depends on the Data Bank rules. Lock useful pieces before reviewing duplicates. Do not merge a valuable main-stat or set combination simply because its monster picture is already in the collection.

sections.title: Why Echoes appear in a terminal
paragraphs: In the game’s setting, a defeated Tacet Discord may leave a Reverberation that can become an Echo through the Terminal’s Data Bank. That connection turns enemy encounters into both exploration progress and equipment collection. The Echo article provides the setting and the combat-equipment explanation; it is a useful companion to the Data Bank page rather than a second character roster.

sections.title: Check before a farming session
paragraphs: Practical checklist: note the desired Echo, required set and main stat, your present Data Bank level, and whether the target area is unlocked. Separate “new collection record” from “usable build upgrade” when judging success. A higher rarity is not automatically the correct equipped piece. Review locked items before any bulk inventory action, and compare the live level panel when a patch changes the system.

history.label: Version 3.0 interface record
history.detail: Kuro’s Version 3.0 notes mention a new Terminal visual effect at Data Bank level 25. This is a dated interface change, not a claim that 25 remains the maximum Data Bank level.

media.label: Data Bank interface reference
media.description: Community reference for the in-game system, its level table and collection records.

sections.title: Keep a working build before experimenting
paragraphs: Echo Presets store an Echo setup for later application. GameBreak workflow suggestion: save the setup you currently use before testing an alternative, give each plan a meaningful role-based name, and write down what you changed. That creates a recoverable comparison instead of a sequence of swaps whose starting point you can no longer reconstruct.

sections.title: Save, apply and compare attributes
paragraphs: Kuro’s documented interface places Echo Preset at the bottom-right of Echo Assembly. Current Setup can be saved as a preset, and the expanded comparison view shows differences between that setup and another preset. This compares configurations; it does not automatically demonstrate the damage of a full team rotation or prove which build is best for your encounter.

sections.title: Where the equipped effects come from
paragraphs: An Echo is both an equipment piece and, when selected in the relevant active position, a source of an Echo ability. Its main stat, substats, cost and Sonata relationship affect the finished build. A saved arrangement should therefore be reviewed as a complete loadout. Changing a visually similar Echo can alter the build even when the monster illustration looks familiar.

sections.title: A quality-of-life feature, not a new item
paragraphs: The official Version 2.1 announcement introduces Echo Preset as a convenience feature. It belongs to equipment management, not to the character’s personal combat talent tree. Keep the feature’s introduction history separate from the release date of a Resonator, Echo or Sonata set. This avoids incorrectly attaching one system’s update date to every item used inside it.

sections.title: Make comparisons fair
paragraphs: Practical checklist: keep the weapon, character level, skill levels, team and enemy fixed. Compare the active Echo skill and full set effects as well as the headline stats. Try the same action sequence with each saved setup and note any Energy or survival issue. A larger single stat is only one observation; record the reason for choosing a preset instead of labeling it universally best.

history.label: Added in the Version 2.1 notes
history.detail: The Version 2.1 notes document saving the current Echo setup, applying presets and expanding attribute comparison. Menu positions can evolve, so use the current client if the layout differs.

sections.title: Learn the transition you keep missing
paragraphs: Resonator Skill Training is a guided place to learn a character’s combat sequence. GameBreak practice suggestion: choose one unfamiliar Resonator, identify the transition that fails, and repeat that part before attempting the entire sequence. Useful goals include recognizing the correct hold input or knowing when a special state is ready. Do not begin by copying another account’s damage total.

sections.title: Find it in the Guidebook
paragraphs: Kuro’s Version 2.5 notes explicitly reference Guidebook → Path of Growth → Skill Training. The community page also describes access from a Resonator’s Forte and attribute screens. If one route is absent, inspect the current character menu and tutorial unlock state rather than assuming the feature is gone. Menu names can differ between interface languages and later updates.

sections.title: Connect the instruction to the character
paragraphs: The tutorial is character-specific rather than a generic equipment recommendation. Read the displayed instruction, perform the required action, and observe which part of the on-screen gauge or animation changes. GameBreak learning suggestion: explain the action in your own words after completing it. Being able to say why the next input becomes available is a better learning signal than merely repeating a button list.

sections.title: Part of the Path of Growth
paragraphs: The Guidebook groups activities that help players learn combat and find progression goals. Skill Training focuses on a Resonator’s sequence, whereas other guidebook activities may serve different purposes. Keep this training record separate from character release history and reward farming. The selected tutorial is the authority for its displayed objective and any reward shown in your current version.

sections.title: Transfer practice into a real encounter
paragraphs: Practical checklist: after finishing the guided sequence, try it against a familiar enemy and add movement, dodging and character switching gradually. A successful scripted tutorial does not prove that the same timing is safe against every boss. Keep the inputs simple at first, note the point where the sequence breaks, and return to that exercise. No in-game testing completion is implied by this reference article.

history.label: Version 2.5 menu evidence
history.detail: Kuro’s Version 2.5 notes mention changing the order of Resonators on the Skill Training screen. That verifies an interface adjustment, not the original launch date of every tutorial.
